previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant was admitted with headache, back pain, and poor appetite. He had been experiencing confusion and tremors, which were linked to elevated tacrolimus levels. An EEG confirmed encephalopathy likely due to medication toxicity. He underwent an ERCP for a biliary stricture, with successful placement of new stents. A urinary tract infection with Pseudomonas was treated with nitrofurantoin, and his kidney function improved. The patient was transitioned from tacrolimus to sirolimus, and his mental status stabilized. Due to ongoing mobility and self-care challenges, he was discharged to a rehabilitation facility with plans for close outpatient monitoring of medication levels and follow-up urine testing.

# Chest Pain
Patient without prior episodes of chest pain. He does have a 
history of GERD for which he takes lansoprazole 30 QD, but 
described this episode as distinct from GERD. Differential 
diagnosis in this patient also included ACS, GERD, PE, 
costochondritis, or diaphragmatic irritation. There was 
suspicion for cardiac etiology, but all data was negative: EKG 
nsl, CXR clear, cardiac enzymes negative x3 (once at OSH and 2x 
in ED). There was some low-level concern for DVT/PE possible 
given mildly asymmetric ___ edema on exam but patient denied SOB 
and calf pain. ___ of the L leg showed no DVT. He was monitored 
on telemetry without complaint. Metoprolol was held in the 
hospital but re-started at discharge. Pain was not explained 
during this admission, nor did it recur. ___ require additional 
outpatient followup.

#Fever.
Patient denied fever or chills prior to OSH presentation, but he 
had a temp of 100.9 there. Afebrile during this admission. In 
him, ddx included infection or thrombus. Given his chief 
complaint of chest pain, would consider PNA or pancreatitis high 
on the differential but CXR clear and lipase wnl. In this 
immunosuppressed patient, we should also consider atypical 
infections, but he showed no sign of infection during this 
admission, apart from a bandemia on ___ count. Urine cultures 
and blood cultures were without growth, HCV viral load pending 
at time of discharge. He was not given any antibiotics or 
additional IVF on the floor. He felt well, eager to go home.

history and admission both non-concerning for bleed: no 
melena/hematochezia, no hematuria, no hematemesis or hemoptysis, 
and no pain on exam that might be concerning for internal 
bleeding. Anemia likely ___ liver failure.

was continued at unchanged doses (sirolimus, myfortic), as was 
bactrim prophylaxis, ursodiol and fenofibrate. Sirolimus was 
continued at pre-admission dose level, but will likely need to 
be adjusted by outpatient providers - the value returned as 
supratherapeutic at >15 after patient was discharged. 
.
#Low back pain
Patient complaining of chronic low back pain, for which he 
already has a specialist f/u appointment. Timeline of back pain 
pre-dates onset of chest pain and fever. he was continued on 
home meds: lidocaine patch + tylenol (max 2 g/day) + ultram PRN.

#Diabetes
